utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Before we hear the evidence of the next witness, there are a couple of matters I'd like to deal with. First, the Chamber will issue an oral ruling in relation to the testimony of Momir Nikolic, who is expected to testify next week. The Chamber notes that in the February list of witnesses filed by the Prosecution on 20th January, Momir Nikolic is listed as a partial Rule 92 ter witness for whom four hours of examination-in-chief were envisaged. In the Rule 92 ter notification filed on 31st of January, the Prosecution reduced this estimated time to two hours but seeks to tender 480 pages of transcript of the witness's testimony in the Tolimir case, which lasted six days. Because of his position as chief of intelligence and security in the Bratunac Brigade during the conflict, Nikolic's evidence is central to the Srebrenica-related allegations charged in the indictment. Therefore, given the nature of Nikolic's testimony, as well as the amount of Rule 92 ter material sought to be tendered through him, the Chamber considers that it is in the interests of justice that he be called viva voce. The Chamber will decide on the time to allocate to the accused for cross-examination once the Prosecution has determined how much time it requires for its examination-in-chief. Turning now to the March and April order of witnesses. The Chamber first notes that Richard Butler is still indicated as a partial Rule 92 ter witness despite the Chamber's order of 8th of December, 2011, that he be called viva voce. The Chamber therefore orders the Prosecution to file a corrected version of the March and April list. Still in relation to the March and April list of witnesses, the Chamber wishes to ask the Prosecution a few clarifying questions in relation to Mr. Dusan Janc and Mr. Dean Manning. First, could the Prosecution clarify whether it wishes to call Janc and Manning pursuant to Rule 92 ter? If so, what prior evidence of statement will be tendered for each of these two witnesses? In that respect, the Chamber also notes that the May 2009 list of witnesses listed them as viva voce witnesses, and for Manning stated that his "reports" will be tendered pursuant to Rule 94 bis. However, the Rule 94 bis dead-line have long passed and no Rule 94 bis filing has been presented. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I don't think it's -- excuse me, Mr. President. I don't think there's any need for any clarification of the inquiry the Court is making. We'll get back to you forthwith with the response to those matters to see if they represent any misunderstanding reflected in the documents on the part of the Prosecution or simply a clerical error, but we'll clarify for the Court forthwith the Prosecution's intentions with respect to both witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tieger. Unless there are any other matters, we'll bring in the next witness. Yes, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. I don't know if this is working. No. Yes. I would just like, if I may, to introduce Ms. Sandra Gudaityte who has joined the stand-by team. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning to you. Ms. West, your next witness is Mr. Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. Do you hear me well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would you take the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Todorovic. Please be seated and make yourself comfortable. Yes, Ms. West.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: What is your name?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: My name is Dragan Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: In Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Sir, can you confirm that you had an opportunity to listen to your testimony in the Popovic case and it accurately reflects your evidence to that Court?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: If you were asked about the same issues today in this court, would you provide the same information?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would tender the Popovic testimony to 65 ter 22406, and there are two associated exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll admit the transcript first.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P4350, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are they -- are there any objections with respect to two associated exhibits, Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. They will be both admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, 65 ter 03827 will be Exhibit P4351 and 65 ter 03826 will be Exhibit P4352 [Realtime transcript read in error "P4353"].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
