utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may read a brief summary. The witness joined the VRS in 1992 and served in other units before joining the 10th Sabotage Unit in late 1994. The 10th Sabotage was under the command of the Main Staff. The witness was responsible for the logistic support of the unit. The 10th Sabotage Unit had two platoons. Todorovic was in the Vlasenica platoon which was based in Dragasevac; and the other bass in Bijeljina. Milorad Pelemis was the commander in the 10th Sabotage, and Pelemis' superiors at the Main Staff were Salapura, Tolimir, and Milanovic and Mladic. Todorovic testified that Petar Salapura was the Main Staff officer who communicated most with the unit. On July 10th, 1995, a written order came from the Main Staff ordering the 10th Sabotage to deploy. The witness packed up equipment and the unit left the base spending the night in Zeleni Jadar. The 10th Sabotage entered Srebrenica on July 11th with orders to capture the town but encountered no resistance. Todorovic saw General Mladic in Srebrenica. The General congratulated the troops, ordered Todorovic and his unit to hold the police station until documents were recovered and ordered the remaining troops on to Potocari. Mladic also told the 10th Sabotage that they had 48 hours to search the town and take what they wanted. The witness returned to the base at Dragasevac the morning of 12th July and the rest of the men from his unit returned in the evening. Commander Pelemis was in charge of the 10th Sabotage Unit throughout the operation in Srebrenica but upon Pelemis's return to the base, Pelemis was injured in a vehicle accident that killed another soldier. Todorovic was tasked with taking the dead soldier killed in the accident back to his family home and attending the funeral. He left Dragasevac on July 13th with several members of his unit. They were gone for two days, returning between 10.00 and 11.00 in the morning July 15th. When Todorovic returned, Pelemis was gone and Todorovic was told that Pelemis was at the hospital in another town. Soon after this, Todorovic saw Pecanac arrive at the base along with a second car. He knew Pecanac was the aide-de-camp to General Mladic and was certain of his identity because Pecanac had, in the past, turned up at the base every now and then, and on this occasion, July 15th, Pecanac entered the base again. Todorovic also recognised the second car, a VW Golf which belonged to Popovic, the security officer for the Drina Corps. Pecanac came on to the base and Todorovic heard Pecanac arguing and shouting with another soldier, Zoran Obrenovic, but the witness did not hear the details. Obrenovic later told the witness that Pecanac ordered him, Obrenovic, to gather troops for a job and that Obrenovic had refused because there was no order coming from Commander Pelemis. Pecanac then shouted at another soldier to round up men for a meeting with Colonel Beara in Zvornik, and that soldier complied. Todorovic then packed equipment for the departing unit. He testified that in addition to normal weapons and combat gear, he issued more additional equipment and ammunition. Seven to eight men from the 10th Sabotage Unit then left with Pecanac in a black VW minivan followed by the Popovic car. Todorovic then went back to Srebrenica with other members of his unit to gather cattle, returned to the base that night and the black minivan was there when he returned, but Todorovic supposed the men were in town at a cafe. On July 16th, Todorovic was in Srebrenica until late in the evening and again did not see the men who had left on the 15th. He had no information about what the men of the 10th Sabotage Unit did on the 15th or the 16th of July.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Mr. Todorovic, I have just a few questions for you. Can you tell the Trial Chamber when the 10th Sabotage Unit was created?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: In 1994, the 1st of November or the 1st of October.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And to whom was the unit subordinated?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: The Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Who was your commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milorad Pelemis was commander of the Sabotage Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And from whom did he receive orders?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: From a higher level, from the Main Staff, from officers.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: I'm now going to show you a video-clip. In total it's about 10 minutes long.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: For the record, this is P4021, the Srebrenica trial video. In the book there are stills that are associated with this video. The video's subtitled as well. The stills start on page 17. There is a transcript as well, but as I said, it's subtitled. For the record, we're starting at minute 23 and 45 seconds, and we will end at minute 33 and 20 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Mr. President, there is sound to this video --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Mr. President, there is sound, and I believe it's being fixed now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would you like it to be played again or we can carry on?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: We can carry on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: We've just stopped at minute 24 and 41 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Mr. Todorovic, on the still in front of you, do you recognise that black uniform we see on the man on the right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And what can you tell us about the patch on the arm?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: It's our patch. It's the patch of my unit, the 10th Sabotage Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: We've stopped at 25 minutes and 10 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: This person we see in the middle who has the black overalls on, do you recognise this person?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: That's a member of the 10th Sabotage Detachment.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please be asked to speak a bit louder. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Todorovic, you are being asked by the interpreters to speak to the microphone or speak up a bit -- turn up your volume a bit. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: We've stopped at 25:37.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: We see a gentleman on the right-hand side. Do you recognise that gentleman?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: General Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you. And we'll continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: We've stopped at 25:53.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Now, we see some soldiers in the middle who have a patch on their arm. Do you recognise that patch?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: There's a wolf on that patch, and they are members of the Drina Corps, the Drina Wolves.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: We'll continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: We've stopped at 26 minutes and 30 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: This man who is standing next to the person you identified as Zivanovic, who is he?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: His brother.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: We'll continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: We've stopped at 29 minutes and 40 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And we saw with the subtitles they were talking about ammunition, and now it says -- they said, "Who is the ammunition for?" "It's for Legenda." Can you tell us who that is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I think he was an officer of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: He had something to do with those Wolves.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: We've stopped at 32 minutes and 37 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: The person who is on the screen now in black, who is that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: That's my commander, the commander of my unit, of the 10th Sabotage Detachment, Milorad Pelemis.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: We'll continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: We're at 32 minutes and 44 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: This man in black as well, was he in your unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And on the screen someone has just said, "Miso, move slowly." Was that Milorad Pelemis's nickname?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: We'll continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: We're at 33 minutes and 3 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Do you recognise this building?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: That's the municipal building in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: What were your orders regarding this building?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: To secure it until all the necessary material that was there was removed.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Did you advance any farther than this building in the town?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No. Up to the police station and the municipal building. We didn't go any further.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: We've concluded at 33 minutes and 20 seconds. Thank you, sir. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. West. Mr. Todorovic -- just a second.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, one correction to the exhibit announced 03826 will be Exhibit P4352 and not P4353. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Todorovic. Your testimony in the Popovic et al. case was admitted here in its entirety in lieu of your examination-in-chief, and you'll be now cross-examined by Mr. Karadzic. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellencies. Good morning to you and everyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: First and foremost, I'd like to thank you for kindly meeting my associates. Therefore, I hope this examination will run smoothly and within the time allocated to us.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I need to remind both of us to pause between question and answer, as it seems I present quite a difficulty for the interpreters because we frequently exchange many words in our language. Could we please both bear that in mind.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You lived in Kladanj; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that in Kladanj there were about 20 per cent of Serbs?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the entire 20 per cent fled at the beginning of the war or on the eve of the war? They all fled from Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Some fled before, some on the very eve of the war, and whoever stayed behind, well, some of them didn't survive, others ended up in a camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So how many Serbs were there in Kladanj who were free in May or June, who were not dead or imprisoned?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Only those who joined the Patriotic League.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You fled on time. In what month?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: In May.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We need to break between questions and answers. After that, was your house in Kladanj set on fire?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: All houses around Kladanj and the villages surrounding Kladanj were attacked and torched.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Before the war were you aware of any Muslim preparations for war in terms of organising the Green Berets and the Patriotic League? Did you have such information? And I do not mean rumours but reliable information.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did the Serb side have any paramilitary formations in Kladanj?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Upon your departure you reported to the Sekovici Brigade. Was that the way you responded to the JNA call-up and was it still at the time when the JNA was a legitimate armed force in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Vlasenica, Sekovici, and the area had a single military post number from the pre-war JNA period. This was continued in the first few months of the war; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You were in the Sekovici Brigade for a while. In the meanwhile, did you join any other forces or units?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us which ones?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: The assault platoon which was formed in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It was all within the JNA structure, and later on when the VRS was formed, it fell within their structure; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You never joined any paramilitary formation on the Serb side in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the JNA and later the VRS conduct any offensive operations in Kladanj and the Serb villages there, or did they provoke an attack on the Serb villages in question?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were there many civilians casualties in those Serb villages?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Out of the total percentage of the population there, there were many dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you specify a number of such villages for the Chamber, the attacked Serb villages in the municipality of Kladanj?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Vucinici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Vucinici. If you look at the screen, you'll be able to observe when the translation of what I said was completed and then you can go on.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Konjevici, Kovacici, Mala and Velika Kula, Vranovici, Mladovo, Pajici, Obrcevac, and all the other villages in that area. I believe this is enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are there any residents in those Serb villages? Did anyone return?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: A very small percentage did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You also went through Janja frequently, which was a majority Muslim settlement in the municipality of Bijeljina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: To be even more accurate, one couldn't get to Bijeljina or Brcko without going through Janja; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was Janja ever attacked by the Serb army?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your municipality of Kladanj, was there a single Serb village that was spared, what was not attacked?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You -- you and the Serbs from the area fled without being able to take anything with you. You only took what was basically on you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When did you join the 10th Sabotage Detachment? It was in the fall of 1992, was it not?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I apologise. 1994. Until 1994, you were still with the Assault Platoon of the Sekovici or Birac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the Special Police of the Sekovici Brigade. I was there for a while as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was the platoon disbanded and another brigade formed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: The Sekovici Platoon was disbanded, and I joined the Vlasenica Intervention Platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you explain for the Chamber the situation in the area given the fact that fighting broke out there somewhat later than in, say, Sarajevo where it all began on the 6th of April? Do you know how the atmosphere there developed in terms of tensions when you arrived there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, there was tension, but nobody mistreated anyone else. No one forced anyone to join the Serb army. There were Muslims there, though, in Vlasenica, quite a percentage of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Am I correct in saying that the Serb youngsters were under an obligation to join the army, whereas the Muslim were not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sekovici and Vlasenica, and Vlasenica is better off economically than Sekovici, but did both settlements receive quite a large number of refugees right at the outset?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Am I correct in saying that all those refugees had fled without being able to take anything with them in haste and that the new municipality of their arrival was supposed to accommodate them in terms of finding places for them to sleep and providing food for those families?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the refugees like you joined the army, whereas the population that was not fit for military service was accommodated in different locations and depended on the municipality for food; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The influx of refugees who told the stories of their lives, did all of that lead to a rise in tensions in Sekovici, and in particular Vlasenica, all the places they were staying at?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to ask you the following: You were in the Territorial Defence -- or, rather, a reservist of the JNA. Did you do your military service before that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Which service?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: The infantry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. After doing your military service, did you become part of the reserve force? Did you get a wartime assignment, as was usually the case with reservists?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It is on that basis that we were called up for military exercises and drills.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you attend such exercises and drills before the war?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On that occasion did you take your uniform home and some weapons and perhaps some noncombat gear, all the things that a soldier has?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we therefore agree that the entire reserve force of the JNA, that is to say, all of those who did their military service, could have some military equipment at home, either uniforms only or also gas masks and small shovels and the like, and some even had rifles and other light weapons; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you joined these units, did you, and if so in which way and how, hear or feel that these units would work on destroying Muslims, killing them or expelling them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: As -- these units were only used for defence in case there was an attack by Muslim units.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. There were lines of separation or confrontation between Sekovici and Kladanj, weren't they? And on the other side, weren't there a lot more Serb villages than there were Muslim villages on this side?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: The line was established. Tuzla, Kladanj, Sarajevo, was the line that followed the road between these towns.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did this line coincide with the ethnic pattern, that is to say where there were Serb majorities and Muslim majorities?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Eighty per cent of Serb villages remained on their side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The Serb army at that point in time and all the way up until the end of the war, did it ever launch any kind of offences against Kladanj with the intention of liberating Kladanj, or were these only defence operations as they tried to link up Kladanj and Drina?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: If we look at the line where the war started, this was the defence line. That is how the war ended. That was the situation at the end of the war too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Without any major shifts in that area. Is that what you're trying to say?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to move on to this other part that we are particularly interested in. Let us first look at the nature of your unit. Is it correct that your unit was mostly used behind enemy lines?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did they also have their own sabotage terrorist groups, as we call them, in our area, behind the lines again?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask you the following: We call those groups sabotage terrorist groups. Do you agree that out of these groups of theirs -- that as far as these groups of theirs are concerned, their victims were mainly civilians on our side and -- on our side and drivers from the bauxite mine and so on and so forth. Our unit, the 10th Sabotage Detachment, did it have permission or orders to kill civilians behind enemy lines?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Not civilians. Just to carry out sabotage and to create confusion on their side and in case of dire necessity to defend itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that between the protected areas, the safe havens, when they were established, and Kladanj civilians did pass? Civilians went to Central Bosnia, and sabotage groups went there all the time, sabotage groups of the Muslim army, and it was necessary to provide security on that road every time when people had to take it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's where they passed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that for quite a long time we tolerated the existence of their units behind our lines, in our rear, far away from the lines, in Kladanj, and for a long time they held under their control Kamenica and other Zvornik villages via Cerska, that is in Vlasenica, and then they also held Konjevic Polje, and they linked up Srebrenica and Kamenica, that entire area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember that at one point in time they attacked vehicles that were transporting bauxite to Zvornik and that they killed the drivers of these vehicles and they seized these trucks? Later on they called this the operation against the Chetniks, but these were actually workers.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At the time when they had this main road under their control, and this entire area, too, we had to go via Sekovici, Crni Vrh and Caparde in order to reach Zvornik; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that there were ambushes on that road, too, and that they would kill, say, all the passengers on a bus and a lot of small passenger cars and that that road was very unsafe too?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That happened at Crni Vrh, because that was the closest road via Memici that led to their own territory. That's how they went back to their own territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to ask you the following: Your unit, would it also be attached at moments -- actually, did it have an anti-terrorist component as well? Was your unit used against these groups of theirs or only in their rear?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It was used depending on how the situation developed on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Then all of a sudden it would receive an assignment, and you as a logistics person would provide food and ammunition for such an operation; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Weapons and leftover ammunition were handed back after an operation. Was the ammunition counted, and was everything registered, the amount of ammunition used and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that the commander, depending on the task he received from the Main Staff, would decide what kind of weapons and ammunition would be issues to the unit, and would he, for example, say that zoljas should be taken or heavy machine-guns? Was he the one who decided on a case-by-case basis?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Between such actions, operations, weapons were kept in storage and members could not go into town armed; right? Unless it was for personal protection and safety.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that this unit had a mixed ethnic composition, that it consisted of Muslims, Croats, even Slovenes? I don't know whether there were any Hungarians there, but I know that there were Hungarians in other units. So was it an ethnically mixed unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that that's the way it was until the very end?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You spoke about that when you testified in Popovic on page 13989. I think that that's the right page reference. Unfortunately, no, I turned this into words, so the page -- actually, I have page 12 out of the 77 pages. Well, anyway, that will be taken care of. Was there a particular culture in that unit, a particular atmosphere? Was there an atmosphere of ethnic intolerance, chauvinism? Was there anything in that unit that would be considered illegal and established as such?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: They were professional -- professionals, just like we were. They were protected. They were a part in the Bijeljina Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that they would not have stayed on in that unit had this unit had a culture of enmity and animosity vis-a-vis other ethnicities?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. To the best of your knowledge, what was the situation in the protected areas in terms of food supply and food production by the peasants themselves, then as far as the passage of convoys was concerned and going out into Serb villages and stealing Serbian cattle?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In a word, were they hungry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. West.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. This was -- this witness's Popovic testimony and the testimony today has nothing to do with the food supply or the convoys. It's beyond the scope.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, the accused is able to put the question about his case if the witness is able to answer, is he not, Ms. West?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour. It's just the way that question was formulated I do not understand it that he was putting his case to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: On a separate note, Ms. West, I just found out there were some parts that were dealt with private session in the Popovic case.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can have a few minutes on that, we will check that out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: First, I know it's page 13999, and about three pages. I'm not sure whether there are further parts that were dealt with in -- dealt with in private session. Could you check it out. Yes, Mr. Karadzic. Could you --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll explain, Excellency, why I'm putting this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please carry on. Mr. Todorovic, do you remember the question? But I would like the accused to reformulate his question. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that in the enclaves there was a life going on, that they had a functioning agriculture throughout, that they had convoys, and in addition to that, they were looting our villages, stealing our cattle? I'm asking that, because at one point of time you were given the task to gather this cattle, and did this cattle actually have to do with their incursions into Serb territory?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: All the convoys that were sent to the enclaves, the protected areas, passed by our check-points unhindered. They were treated with maximum fairness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: As for their incursions in our villages, they took whatever they could find, which means at Christmas not a single pig was left for roasting, and yet they don't eat pork. As for any other cattle, they would pick up anything they found.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that military activity outside Zepa and Srebrenica was constant despite the fact that these were protected areas, and are you aware of such incursions into our villages?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: There was Kravica, and the attack came from the protected area. It was led by Naser Oric. Everyone knows how those people were killed and mutilated. There are documents which speak to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You were accommodated in Vlasenica for the most part; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you know of their excursions, so to say, in Milici as well.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The mine there.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpret's correction: The village is called Rudnik and up to Derventa.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll share with you a few dates from their documents. I won't go to the period before May, because you were still not in the area; correct.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But we were there with the assault detachment as well when they came in for the first time, when they killed the drivers and workers at the mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the 2nd of June, it seems there was a sabotage action carried out on the road against the -- against the soldiers. Was the village in question Drum near Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Drum was inhabited by Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So their attack came from there and then they opened fire at the command?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: They opened fire on the Panorama Hotel where there were JNA officers as well Serb personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us go to 1995. I have a plan here of the Drina Corps for June 1995. It seems to be for June. There is no mention whatsoever of any operation against Srebrenica. Did you know that Srebrenica was to be captured, and do you agree that the first and foremost task was to sever the enclaves of Srebrenica and Zepa because they linked them up unlawfully?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Mr. President, if we can just have a cite for a plan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, and put one question at a time, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I apologise to the Prosecution. I will have the document registered or tendered through one of the next witnesses, perhaps over the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So do you agree that at the time the first and main task was to return the Muslims within the boundaries of defined protected areas and to free the route between Milici and Skelani; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that because of the fact that they linked up their enclaves between Milici and Skelani, instead of travelling 50 kilometres from one point to the next one had to go the roundabout way, which took about 150 kilometres?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You were sent to Srebrenica. Is it true that it was customary that your commander would tell you your task immediately prior to its execution?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You entered Srebrenica on the 11th of July, sometime in the afternoon. When did you enter Srebrenica exactly?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, around noon or early in the afternoon. We split at Zeleni Jadar into two combat groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When did you arrive in Zeleni Jadar?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: On the 10th in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know that before the 10th, starting with the 5th, there was fighting to the south of Srebrenica in the area of Zeleni Jadar, that is to say, between Zepa and Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were trying to defend the road, the route they had for the supply of weapons into Zepa and the other way. They smuggled weapons and food as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Once you arrived there, basically none of that resistance was left; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you have any information as to what was going on with their killed soldiers? Were they buried by our army before your arrival? The casualties who were killed the week before, starting with the 5th, did they have casualties?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Not in our area of responsibility. There were no casualties there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, when you arrived, but how about before that when they were still trying to defend the area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, possibly. I'm certain there were casualties on both sides. It's a forested area, but I didn't go in that part of the field.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I note the time. If it is convenient, we'll take a break now for 20 minutes. We will resume at 10.40.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. West.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. We have uploaded a public redacted version of the Popovic testimony. That number is 65 ter 22406A. I thank you for your correction. I did notice one other page. That mistake is mine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So shall we give the separate number for the public redacted version.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, P4353.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Karadzic. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that you as a person in charge of logistics were not privy to operational documents and that the documents you worked with had to do with the needs of the unit per task?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that you never heard or were present when Pelemis received any records from an officer of the Main Staff? Perhaps you saw him talking to someone, but you didn't hear any specific orders he may have received; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said so in 2004 as well, but perhaps there is no need to call up those documents. Let us go back to your entry in Srebrenica. You entered on the 11th. Is it true that in the town of Srebrenica there were neither their army nor their population?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: There were none along the axis we came in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In other words, they left Srebrenica, and your entry in Srebrenica was not a violent one. There was no shooting or people being killed; correct? I mean the entry down into Srebrenica itself.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me ask you something about a footage we saw. At 2510, it seems we saw one of your soldiers with a headband. Was it customary that soldiers wear unconventional items like that, or did other soldiers have those headbands as well? Would you like me to replay it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No. I guess people wore it for the sake of their image, at least as far as our soldiers were concerned. As for the Muslim soldiers, they had headbands which said "tekbir Allahu akbar." All of their soldiers wore such headbands as well as their mercenaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Tekbir. It seems we have a problem with the Turkish term.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Allahu akbar. It was their combat cry, whenever they attacked our fortifications or villages. Who did they fight for? For Allah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If such a headband were in a grave for a while could the text disappear and the band remain, actually?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, it all depended on the quality of the fabric.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. West.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: This is not a witness for that answer, and also it calls for speculation. He would have no basis to answer a question like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Absolutely, Ms. West. Please move on, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At 25:53 we see that in addition to the shoulder patch, a soldier also had a red ribbon. Was it customary to wear such ribbons to prevent any friendly fire?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is how we distinguished our soldiers among themselves from the enemy so that they wouldn't start shooting at each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you change the colour of such ribbons daily so that the enemy couldn't imitate it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: It depended on the situation where the soldiers were, and we were able to change it every day so that the enemy would be unable to know what we wore on what day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At 30 minutes, we hear Mladic mention the Dahijas. Since those participating in the proceedings need not necessarily know what it is, can you please confirm or deny this. Do you agree that the Dahijas rebelled against the Sultan as well as against the Serb local authorities during the Turkish occupation and that they were the evil kind who even disobeyed the Sultan's laws?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The Dahijas were renegades. They committed crimes and did not report to either the Sultan or the Agas or Begs who were other Turkish aristocracy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that Milenko Stojkovic killed them in the end and that Karadjordje received the Sultan's approval for that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: In these crimes and outrages, was Naser Oric a modern-day Dahija, as it were?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, chance had it that I had occasion to also talk with people who were members of his unit, so he was not very friendly to his own people and arrogant with his own people, let alone others.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, did you understand that they were actually revenging on the population or was it on the Dahijas, or, rather, the Oric men? Well, it is not accidental that he mentioned the Dahijas when referring to Oric's territory.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Those people had wreaked a lot of evil to the people and the population around Srebrenica, Milici, Vlasenica. There were thousands of victims that were in fact at the hands of Naser's commanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, when you entered Srebrenica, there was no shelling or shooting in any real sense of the word; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, the video that we were shown, we can see that there was some sporadic fire and that Mladic asked where the fire was coming from. Was that shooting actually coming from the Muslim side? Well, maybe you don't know. If you don't know, just say so.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I do know. Many of those units actually went into the woods, and for another month or so they still terrorised the population in the area. They would break into Serbian villages and they would destroy everything that was in their way. They were trying to break through to Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. We didn't get any interpretation. With respect to the previous question, I'm not sure whether we heard your answer to the question whether the sporadic fire we saw or heard in the video were coming from the Muslim side. Mr. Todorovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But you confirmed that the -- they went into the woods to break into Serbian villages. So you are saying to us that they were firing from the woods against the Serbs who were entering the Srebrenica town. Is that what you're saying, Mr. Todorovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I don't think we got translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. I will repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, there was renegade groups. They were actually broken-up groups, stragglers, and they were on the periphery of Srebrenica, the outskirts of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you mentioned Milici. Is it correct that they engaged our units on their way, on their attempt to break through, and where our units were deployed, they attacked Serb villages and killed civilians?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Below Milici, there is -- on the way out of Milici there is a house there. Fortunately, there -- well, there was a whole family there that they killed. Fortunately, they did not -- their son was not there, so they didn't end the line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, let me just ask you whether you saw any signs of the fighting, the destruction? Did you see any destruction in Srebrenica itself? In other words, did Srebrenica suffer a lot of devastation in this operation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: As for our movement through Srebrenica and my unit, the Sabotage Detachment and other units as well, not a single house was torched, although we did search every house in order to try to determine whether any of their soldiers actually changed into civilian clothing. We wanted to make sure as we were passing through that none of them would be left behind so they could open fire behind our backs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just one more clarifying question, Mr. Todorovic. In your previous answer as regards the Muslim forces, you said many of those units went into the woods and for a month they still terrorised the population in the area. Do you remember having said that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What population were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, whenever they tried to break through in order to link up with Tuzla via Crni Vrh, Baljkovica, the road going across or over Cerska, Kamenica, Memici. Whenever they came to Serb villages, they killed in order to loot their clothes or bandages or civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So in addition to the group that pulled out by the 16th of July, there were some straggling groups in that area; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, the group that was led out by Tursunovic, they went via Baljkovica, and they killed members of the Drina Brigade there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, did you have any information as to how fierce that fighting was, that it was so fierce that, for instance, the Zvornik Brigade lost more men during this breakout attempt of theirs than through the entire war period?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At one point, and I'll tell you exactly where, you said that General Mladic said, and that's on page 14005 of this transcript that was admitted into evidence, that Mladic said that you should withdraw and that you had 48 hours at your disposal to search everything and take whatever you wanted. Is it correct that that did not refer to private property but, rather, to the equipment that was the property of the 28th Division?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Precisely so. Only stuff that we found such as weapons, uniforms, insignia. In other words, things that we might want as trophies or souvenirs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When was it then that you left Srebrenica after you entered it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I left Srebrenica on the 12th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was that in the early hours?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, around 10.00, 11.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While you were there, there was no killing, no bombing, nothing extraordinary, nothing critical; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No. Only on the 11th we were bombed by aircraft.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You were in charge of collecting cattle, and that's the cattle that was roaming in the areas because they were deserted.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. This was the looted private property. The cattle was looted from villagers, because there were a lot of people there who did nothing other than go around looting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When did Major Pecanac arrive? The transcript does not reflect that this was cattle that was looted from Serb villages. That's what you said, correct, that they were lotted from our villages?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Major Pecanac, who may have been a captain at the time, arrived then and he came to your base; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You saw the vehicle that was usually driven by Vujadin Popovic on that occasion; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, you could not identify him with certainty as the driver. You knew that there was a -- there was someone in the vehicle, but you couldn't identify whether it was him or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, that's correct. It was his vehicle, but whether he was driving the car or not, I really don't know. It is possible, but it's also possible that it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Pecanac -- or, rather, who was it who stood in for your commander while he was absent?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, whoever had the rank at the time. A combat group leader or someone like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And he addressed whom?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: He addressed Obrenovic, and I later found out why, but at the time when they were having this conversation, I was not there. I did not dare walk up to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Oh, I see. So you just heard their quarrel, but you couldn't really make out what it was that they were quarreling about; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: He then spoke to Gojkovic, because Obrenovic turned him down. He said that he wouldn't do it because the commander wasn't there; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then he turned to Gojkovic and asked for several soldiers because they had to go on a mission; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Franc Kos, who was the lieutenant, did -- was he at the base at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and he took up a -- upon himself this role.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was Franc Kos a Slovene?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was Drazen Erdemovic there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Erdemovic was with me in Trebinje, but he volunteered. He was not forced to go. And he was a sergeant. That's -- that was his rank.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, do you agree that this was on the 15th?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember that at the request of the civilian authorities from Srebrenica, Skelani, Bratunac, on the 14th I declared a state of war, although the fighting around Srebrenica had already ended. And the reason that was done was because of all these straggling groups that were still in the woods.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Those groups killed four men from Milici in Kupusina, I believe. That's in the direction of Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that they were -- that had they organised themselves well, they could have taken any town they wanted, these 13- to 15.000 men who headed for Tuzla? Is it correct that the threat from them was real?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, they knew the defences of our lines, and they knew how they were not too well defended, so they could take any area there. With 15.000 men, they could go in any direction.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The witness mentioned some places that I didn't catch.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The interpreters noted they didn't catch some of the names of the places Mr. Todorovic said. Could you repeat the names of the places?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, this group -- or, rather, this formation of 15.000 men, they were able to capture Milici, Vlasenica, and the entire road through towards Kladanj, but also towards Zvornik and Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to ask you this. As always, not knowing the details of the operation, you issued certain equipment to them; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could we now please see the list of the issued equipment, and I believe this is in one of the associate exhibits. Let me ask you this: Is it correct that you issued a machine-gun, M-84 machine-gun, ammunition for this machine-gun, as well as ammunition for automatic rifles?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. There was also a zolja and a small mortar, shells, water, blankets, sleeping bags and other stuff that they needed for 48 hours, such as food, water, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that they were also issued rations and cans of food, and is it correct that they were equipped for survival basically outside of any human settlements?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's absolutely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So if they had -- if their mission was to execute some individuals, would they need cans of food, blankets, water, and other items that you would need if you were to spend some time in uninhabited places, or if they had been assigned such a task, would they go to towns and obtain their own necessities there? In other words, were they equipped for some period of time that they would spend in an inhabited area or uninhabited areas, in the field as it were?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, they were equipped to spend 48 hours or up to 48 hours wherever they found themselves, whether they had to secure a road, whether they had to escort someone or spend some time in the woods, anything of that sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know which direction they went?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: There are several directions there. The first one was when they moved from the base to Sekovici. Then there is another branch leading to Kladanj and then Trnovo --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please slow down, notes the interpreter. We cannot follow this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The interpreter could not follow. Could you repeat from the start.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This unit, once it left the compound, the base, that is, they took the road towards Sekovici. However, part of the road leads to Kladanj, so they could have taken that part. Then also they could have also gone to Trnovo, Pelemisi, Memici, Osmaci, Crni Vrh, Baljkovica, Zvornik. So they could have gotten anywhere moving in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But they set out from Vlasenica to the left, westward toward Sekovici. Now, let me ask you this: If they were supposed to reach Zvornik as soon as possible would they have taken a different route, towards Nova Kasaba?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That's the main road, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's the main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Whereas Crni Vrh, Caparde, et cetera, that road is a roundabout road, but that was where the breakthrough of the Muslim units took place.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is where Naser broke through.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Commander Pelemis, when entering Srebrenica, did he issue some instructions or orders in relation to what lay in store for you there and in terms of what you should do?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Before each and every operation, my commander would line up the detachment and issue orders saying that we should take care of one another, that we should take care of ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did he tell you that their soldiers had changed into civilian clothing, a large number of them who had now gone into the woods, and that you should be careful so as not to be killed by one of them?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not hear an answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you repeat your answer, Mr. Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which answer? This last one you mean?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean when Pelemis is lining up people, the entire detachment, before an operation, drawing the attention of all soldiers to the fact that they should take care of themselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did he tell you about the soldiers who changed into civilian clothing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ah. That is something that he particularly drew our attention to, because he's an experienced officer, and he spent a lot of time at the front line, and he said that that kind of things happens in 90 per cent of all situations, when people go into towns, that they change their clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did he say anything about treating civilians, Muslim civilians, who were assumed to have been in Srebrenica still?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: If we were to come across any civilians or military-aged soldiers, we were to get close to them. There should be proper security, and these people should be taken to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was there an explicit ban on inflicting any kind of suffering on civilians?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Every time when the unit would get lined up, that was referred to. When civilians did not put up any resistance, no one could touch them. It was only if soldiers took action against us then we should respond in kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. While you were in Srebrenica, you saw many civilians in Potocari. Did you go to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No. I saw that in the media. We only came to the police station and the municipality. That's where we provided security, and that was the end of any kind of combat activity of my unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the proofing note that the OTP sent this morning, it says that you did not see any victims except for one body that wore NATO camouflage uniform and that you thought that this may have been a Serb, and later on this turned out to be a Muslim; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Four or five bodies that did appear on the film. Did you not see any of that.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I saw that, but that was on the 12th when our unit was not involved in combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that in addition to Erdemovic who was a Croat there was also a Mladen who was also a Croat in your unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Mladjo was his nickname.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that this Dreza and his family had also fled from Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were staying at Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can it be said that most of the members of your unit had been relocated or, rather, had fled from somewhere?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You also gave and statement to the FBI; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How did that happen? How come they expressed interest?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Witness is not in the position to answer that question, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, that's in the transcript. It's page 14019, line 8. I don't see why the objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's upload at that page.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Line 8.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Mr. President, the fact -- the fact of the interview is there, but the question that was asked is not one in which this witness can answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. The part Ms. West objected to was the question: "How come they expressed interest?" You didn't ask the witness what he heard from them but the intention of the FBI. But I'm fine with you putting the passage to the witness and ask a question. Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I think that sometimes when someone is interviewing a person they tell them the reason why they're conducting that interview. So it seems like if the witness could answer --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, he can ask whether he heard anything, but he can reformulate his question. Yes, Mr. Karadzic, what is your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you find this unusual, that a US investigation agency was expressing interest in interviewing you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: At first glance, yes, but later on when Boskic fell in America -- he was a member of the sabotage detachment --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I see. Thank you. So that had to do with that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, he fell there in America as a member of the 10th Sabotage Detachment. I really don't know what he said there. Maybe they needed to compare something to his statement or whatever.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We have great trouble hearing Mr. Karadzic. Could he please speak into the microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you repeat your question, and please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On page 14028, you said that Pecanac was refused soldiers, and that was due to the fact that there was no commander -- or, rather, the commander was not there to issue any orders, and we do not have any proof of that being due to the nature of the mission involved; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. The only proper order would have come from Commander Pelemis to send -- to send the unit out into the field. One always acted in accordance with his orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The quantities of material that you issued to this group from the unit on the 15th, were they any different from the usual kind of supplies that you issued?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: That was always prepared when a combat group was going out into the field. Because no one could foresee what would happen in the field, what the unit or the combat group would do out in the field, whether they would be spending the night out there. Did they have to be provided with various equipment so that they could stay there safely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On page 14041, from line 11 onwards, you said that there were ABiH members everywhere, and you also refer to the breakthroughs that you told us about a moment ago. All of that is on that page, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The cattle that you had gathered previously had been stolen from us. You said that on page 14043; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When did you hear -- or, rather, did you hear of large numbers of casualties all over the place during that breakthrough?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And did you hear, and if so how, of any unlawful killings, liquidations?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: That's when the arrests of my unit started.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And that was when, a few years after that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. It was in the media, but, you know, the media will be the media, newspapers and whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you didn't trust the media. Do you remember that the media also said that in Cerska in 1993, blood was flowing down the streets, that there were massacres there? Is that the kind the propaganda that led you to disregard the media?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. When that happened in Cerska, they killed 28 or 29 people from Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour, relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Ms. West?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: I object to these media questions for relevance reasons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think it's related to his attitude towards media clippings. But in any event, he answered the question. We can move on. But, Mr. Todorovic -- oh, yes. In answer to the question about the possibility of any unlawful -- unlawful killings, you answered you heard about it for the first time "when the arrest of my unit started." What did you mean by the arrest of your unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, when there were these proceedings against them. Then I heard that they had allegedly been there. That's as far as the members of my unit are concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you tell us in more concrete terms what -- what happened, in particular your unit's arrest.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Erdemovic was arrested and then he opened this case of Pilica something. I could not have assumed that these soldiers had been there. Then Branjevo. Afterwards, Marko Boskic was arrested in America. He also said that he was forced to be in some army and forced to do something, and that was not correct. Also, Erdemovic also said that he was forced to do something at gunpoint. That's not true. Whoever would have made him doing anything but at gunpoint would have had to answer for it later before the commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So by arrest of your unit, you meant arrest of Erdemovic and Boskic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Erdemovic, Boskic, Kos, Golijan, Savanovic, Cvetkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I understood. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I just wanted to remind you -- or, rather, to see whether you disregarded the media because there were similar propaganda every time when there was some kind of fighting and that Cerska had been declared to have been the site of a massacre and none of that had ever happened?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that before the protected area of Srebrenica was declared it had also been marked as a massacre location by the world media and that our operations were then stopped and it was still back in 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. I have no further questions of you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karadzic. Yes, Ms. West. Do you have any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Very brief.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Sir, today at about transcript page 31, you were talking about hearing firing on the video. Mr. Karadzic asked you a couple of questions and then Judge Kwon did as well. Do you remember those questions?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And that firing that we heard on the video, when you were there, in fact, you didn't see somebody firing from the woods, did you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No, no. But it was coming from somewhere else. We were already in the town itself, and chances are that it was the Muslim army firing unless some Serbs were already celebrating the liberation of Srebrenica. It is my assumption though that their groups had been broken up and that they were in the outskirts of the town or in the forests already.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Okay. And that's what I want to ask you about. Can you tell us what happy fire is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, some soldiers got drunk even at home, let alone out in the field or at the front line.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And let me ask you again. Can you -- can you tell me exactly what happy fire is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Rejoicing. You put a magazine, a cartridge of 30 bullets in your rifle and fire them in the air sort of to make it -- to relieve yourself, in a way, of tension.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: All right. And on this video we saw a number of soldiers from the 10th Sabotage and we also saw some Drina Wolves soldiers as well, but was it the case that there were also other soldiers in the area that we could not see on the video?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Of course. It was an operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you. I have nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Todorovic, that concludes your evidence today, and on my -- on behalf of this Chamber and the Tribunal as a whole, I would like to thank you for your coming to The Hague again to give it. Now you are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. West, do you need a break for -- for the preparation of the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: But if we have -- may we go into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I heard that the next witness is to be heard in closed session.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So we better go into closed session right now.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go into closed session.
